added.message:
Patch Set 7:

PS7 on top of PS6: fixes for the items listed in the PS6 review.

1. llvm provides llvm-xray and llvm-prof-tools, and clang provides clang-analyzer (= %{version}-%{release}). The Obsoletes bound is now "<", so a package never obsoletes its own Provides.
2. The scan-build report resources (/usr/share/scan-build) and its man page move from llvm-devel to clang. The scan-view data (/usr/share/scan-view) moves from llvm-devel to llvm, next to scan-view.
3. libscanbuild and libear are no longer removed in %install and are shipped in clang, so analyze-build, intercept-build and scan-build-py can import them. No Python runtime requirement is added to any package.
4. The six installed scripts that start with "#!/usr/bin/env python" (scan-view, run-find-all-symbols.py and four opt-viewer scripts) are switched to python3 in %install, followed by a check that fails the build if a rewrite does not apply.
5. Your item 3: the OpenMP symlink comment now describes the actual install directory. Your item 5: #undef for the helper macros and the is16BitMemOperand alignment in X86BoltMnemonicTables.cpp.
6. The commit message body is rewritten to describe the change against the base.

Tested on x86_64: full llvm build, with the file lists of all packages matching the intended moves and the clang Requires unchanged. With only clang, llvm and libllvm installed (no llvm-devel), scan-build writes its HTML report, and scan-view, analyze-build, intercept-build and scan-build-py --help run. The opt-viewer scripts still need the optional yaml and pygments Python modules, which are not part of the base.
